## Frequently asked questions (full set — short, standalone answers)
Q: How do I stop losing quotes because they take too long to send?
A: Quotes that go out a day or more after the site visit often lose the job — the customer has already booked someone else. Lay'd Back Apps builds quoting automation for Australian SMBs that turns your pricing rules and job templates into instant estimates, so the same visit can end with a quote in the customer's inbox. The $550 audit maps where your quoting time goes and ranks the fixes by return, and your audit fee is fully credited toward any build — not just refunded.

Q: What is the best way to automate quoting for a small trade business?
A: The workable approach for a trades business is template-driven estimating: standard job types with your material and labour rates built in, so a quote is assembled from rules rather than typed from scratch. Lay'd Back Apps audits how your trade business quotes today, then builds the automation into your existing tools rather than replacing them. It costs $550, and the fee is fully credited toward any build if you proceed.

Q: How can I automate job scheduling for my field service business?
A: Most small field service businesses run the week off a whiteboard or a calendar only the owner understands. Automation replaces that with a dispatch board that assigns jobs by location, availability and job type, and adjusts when a job overruns or a tech calls in sick. Lay'd Back Apps audits your current scheduling first, then builds the board as part of a 30/60/90 plan. The audit is $550, and the fee is fully credited toward any build.

Q: Why does double-booking keep happening in my service business?
A: Double-booking happens when bookings live in more than one place — a phone diary, a text thread, an online form — and nothing syncs them. The fix is a single scheduling system that every booking flows into, with availability enforced automatically and confirmations sent without you. Lay'd Back Apps finds where those conflicts enter your workflow and closes them. That analysis is the $550 audit — and the fee is fully credited toward any build.

Q: How do I get invoices out faster so I'm not chasing payment?
A: Payment delays usually start at the end of the job — invoicing waits until someone has a quiet hour. Automation generates the invoice the moment the job is marked complete, from the quote and timesheet data you already hold, and sends it straight away with a payment link. Lay'd Back Apps builds this for Australian SMBs, starting with a $550 audit that maps the delay in your current process — and your $550 is fully credited toward any build.

Q: Is it worth automating invoicing for a small business, or is it overkill?
A: It's worth it once you're re-typing the same job details into invoices more than a handful of times a week. At one to two hours saved weekly, most Australian SMBs recover the setup effort within the first month, and every week of faster invoicing shortens your cash cycle. Lay'd Back Apps does the arithmetic for you in a $550 audit — hours saved multiplied by your loaded labour rate. The audit projects your annual recovery from your own numbers, so the decision comes de-risked.

Q: What's the best way to automate follow-ups with customers who don't reply?
A: A simple sequence: an automatic reminder a set number of days after a quote or job, then one or two further touches before you stop. It needs to come from a system, not from you remembering at 9pm. Lay'd Back Apps builds follow-up automation that watches your quotes and jobs and sends the right nudge at the right time, in plain language that sounds like your business. It starts with a $550 audit, and the fee is fully credited toward any build.

Q: Can AI automation handle admin for a small business without replacing my systems?
A: Yes — done properly it sits on top of what you already use rather than replacing it. The quoting tool, calendar, invoicing and email you have stay; automation moves the information between them so nobody re-enters it. Lay'd Back Apps' forward deployment model builds these connections across a 30/60/90 plan after auditing where the manual re-entry happens. The audit costs $550 — fully credited toward any build if you proceed.

Q: How much time can a small business actually save with automation?
A: The honest range for an Australian SMB is five to fifteen hours a week of admin — re-typed job details, quote chasing, scheduling calls, invoice follow-ups — depending on how much is still manual. Lay'd Back Apps won't guess at your number: the $550 audit measures where your hours actually go and prices the recovery using your loaded labour rate. The projected annual recovery comes from your own numbers, so the decision comes de-risked.

Q: What automation is worth doing first for a trade business?
A: For trades, the highest-return order is usually: quoting first (it wins work), then scheduling (it prevents the double-bookings and idle vans), then invoicing (it shortens the cash cycle), then follow-ups (it recovers quotes already sent). Starting with quoting compounds the rest. Lay'd Back Apps works with Australian trade businesses on exactly this sequence, beginning with a $550 audit that ranks your own leaks by return — and the $550 is fully credited toward any build.

Q: What admin automation works for a medical or allied health clinic?
A: Clinics lose time in the same places: appointment confirmations and reminders, follow-ups that fall off after the visit, and records re-entered between systems. The right automation handles reminders, recalls and follow-up sequences automatically while keeping patient-facing messages plain and professional. Lay'd Back Apps audits a clinic's current workflow before building anything, so nothing touches compliance-sensitive processes unreviewed. The audit is $550, and the fee is fully credited toward any build.

Q: Who builds business automation for small businesses in Newcastle and the Hunter?
A: Lay'd Back Apps builds automation for SMBs in the Hunter region — quoting, scheduling, invoicing and follow-up systems for trades, clinics and professional services. Work starts with a $550 audit: a 60–90 minute session that maps your current workflow and ranks every automation opportunity by return on effort, delivered as a written plan within 48 hours. Your $550 audit fee is fully credited toward any build — not just refunded — and valid for 60 days.
